description: A table function may be used directly as a FROM source only under LATERAL: FROM t, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ','). Live-measured: without the LATERAL keyword - a bare FROM fn(...) or FROM t, fn(...) - Snowflake raises a syntax error, and only the TABLE(fn(...)) wrapper works in that position. Frostlake matches both sides. The bare LATERAL form correlates per row and produces exactly what the TABLE()-wrapped form produces; GENERATOR takes no left correlation but still needs the keyword in the bare form, so FROM t, LATERAL GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 2) is a 3x2 cross product. Converted 1:1 from query/BareLateralTableFunctionTest (now retired); the Java compared the bare and wrapped forms row by row in Java, which the converted test states as EXCEPT in both directions plus a row-count equality - a set comparison that cannot pass by both sides being empty.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
SELECT t.id, f.value FROM t, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',') f ORDER BY t.id, f.index
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT t.id, f.value FROM t, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',') f EXCEPT SELECT t.id, f.value FROM t, TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',')) f)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT t.id, f.value FROM t, TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',')) f EXCEPT SELECT t.id, f.value FROM t, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',') f)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',') f
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t, TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',')) f
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t, LATERAL GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 2)
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, s VARCHAR)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t, SPLIT_TO_TABLE(t.s, ',') f
SELECT value FROM TABLE(SPLIT_TO_TABLE('x,y,z', ',')) ORDER BY index
